title: Why Submarines Implode In Less Than 1 Millisecond

scenes.name: Crushing Hydrostatic Abyss
scenes.narration: At twelve thousand feet below the surface, the water pressure on a submarine hull is equal to the weight of the Empire State Building.

scenes.name: Microscopic Delamination
scenes.narration: If repeated deep dives create microscopic cracks between the carbon fiber layers, the hull's structural integrity is compromised.

scenes.name: Instantaneous Buckling
scenes.narration: When the shell finally buckles, the colossal pressure punches inward at over fifteen hundred miles per hour.

scenes.name: Adiabatic Compression Fire
scenes.narration: As the air inside is compressed into a tiny space in milliseconds, it instantly superheats to the temperature of the surface of the sun.

scenes.name: Human Neural Latency
scenes.narration: Because human nerves require one hundred milliseconds to register pain, the passengers are vaporized before they can even perceive the sound.
